title: An introductory email
prompt: Write an email introducing yourself to a new classmate. Explain how you know a mutual friend and suggest a meeting.
checks: I included a greeting and a closing.
I introduced myself and explained the connection.
I used be and possessive forms correctly.
I used capitals for names, places and I.

title: My work or study routine
prompt: Write a short blog post about a useful work or study routine. Give your opinion and include frequency words.
checks: I used do, have or make collocations.
I put frequency words in the correct position.
I checked simple present verb endings.
I explained why the routine helps.

title: A bike ride or exercise plan
prompt: Describe a bike ride or an exercise activity. Explain what people usually do and what is happening today. Join ideas with and, but and so.
checks: I distinguished a routine from an activity happening now.
I used sports or exercise words.
I connected ideas with and, but and so.
I checked am/is/are + verb-ing.

title: An invitation and a reply
prompt: Write an invitation to a festival, concert or party, then a reply. Include a day, time, place and arrangements.
checks: I gave the day, time and place.
I used the present continuous for an arrangement.
My reply accepts or declines politely.
I used object pronouns clearly.

title: A memorable first experience
prompt: Describe a first experience or a trip. Explain what happened, how you felt and how you reacted.
checks: I described events in the simple past.
I included feelings and reactions.
I checked did/did not + base verb.
I included details that explain why it mattered.

title: A shopping experience
prompt: Write about a shopping experience or plan. Describe the store, the things you chose and how you used your money. Use one or ones to avoid repetition.
checks: I used money and shopping words.
I used going to for a plan where appropriate.
I used one/ones clearly.
I checked all/most/some/none.

title: My point of view about food
prompt: Write an opinion about a food or eating habit. Give reasons and examples. Describe ingredients or taste and what you enjoy or would like to try.
checks: I stated a clear point of view.
I gave reasons or examples.
I checked count/noncount quantifiers.
I used -ing or to + verb correctly.

title: Advice for a new international student
prompt: Write advice for a student moving to your city. Include transportation, making friends and solving a problem. Use if/when and to/for.
checks: I made useful suggestions.
I used if/when for a situation.
I checked to + verb and for + noun.
I explained how the advice helps.

title: An advertisement
prompt: Create a short advertisement for an invented shop or product. Use comparisons and a superlative to make it appealing. State an offer clearly.
checks: I described the product clearly.
I used a comparative with than.
I used a superlative correctly.
I gave clear details about the offer.

title: An email about a new role
prompt: Write an email about a new job or volunteer role. Describe duties, possible challenges and plans. Add information with by the way and return to your topic with anyway.
checks: I described duties with have to.
I distinguished certainty from possibility.
I used by the way and anyway appropriately.
I included a clear greeting and closing.

title: Advice for online life
prompt: Write a short post giving advice about taking photos or using social media. Describe an experience and use when to explain what to do in a situation.
checks: I used present perfect for an experience.
I used simple past with a finished time.
I used when to connect a situation and advice.
My advice uses clear internet vocabulary.

title: A community garden plan
prompt: Write a plan to turn an empty space into a shared garden. Explain the place, the people and the steps, using first, then, next and finally.
checks: I described the place and people.
I used who/which/that clearly.
I sequenced the steps.
I explained why the project would help.
